name: Context7 MCP
why: Version-specific library references when an agent lacks a docs connector.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node 20.18.1+ and npx. Optional CONTEXT7_API_KEY for higher rate limits.

setup.label: Transport
setup.detail: Runs locally and sends documentation queries to Context7.

cautions: Queries leave the machine. Rate limits and service plans apply.

name: Playwright MCP
why: Useful for interactive UI checks and inspecting application behavior.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node 20+; browser binaries may need downloading.

setup.label: Profile
setup.detail: Default persistent profile retains logins; --isolated uses a fresh session.

cautions: Browser actions can change live data; duplicate existing browser tools only when needed.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
description: Inspect and debug Chrome using DevTools.
why: Use performance traces, network inspection and browser debugging when needed.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node LTS, npm, current stable Chrome.

setup.label: Transport
setup.detail: Runs a local stdio server and controls Chrome.

cautions: Browser contents and logged-in sessions may be exposed to the agent; overlaps Playwright.
Google collects usage statistics by default; --no-usage-statistics opts out. The server also checks npm for updates by default.

name: Next.js DevTools MCP
description: Inspect a running Next.js development server.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node 20.19+ LTS and Next.js 16+ running dev server for runtime tools.

setup.label: Setup
setup.detail: Start the project development server separately.

cautions: Do not enable for projects without the required Next.js version.

name: shadcn/ui MCP
why: Use in a project that already uses shadcn/ui registries.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node and npx. Registry settings come from the project components.json.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: Public registry needs no key; private registries may need credentials.

cautions: Installing components changes project files and dependencies. Check third-party registries before using them.

name: Cloudflare API MCP
description: Call Cloudflare APIs through hosted MCP.
why: For Cloudflare account operations when an MCP connection is desired.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: Cloudflare account and client-supported OAuth, or a scoped API token configured manually.

setup.label: Permissions
setup.detail: Select only required scopes; existing account permissions and product billing apply.

cautions: Permitted calls can modify live infrastructure. OAuth is a separate user action.

name: Cloudflare Docs MCP
why: Focused Cloudflare documentation lookup where general search is inadequate.

setup.label: Transport
setup.detail: Connects to the hosted documentation server.

cautions: Overlaps Context7 and web search.

name: Cloudflare CLI
description: Manage Cloudflare API resources and Workers projects.
why: Terminal-native Cloudflare operations and command discovery.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node 22.18+; cf is beta.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: Run cf auth login to sign in. Use cf auth whoami to check the account.

cautions: Commands can change live resources. Product fees and access controls apply.

name: Cloudflare Wrangler
why: Prefer the project-local CLI in existing Wrangler projects.

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Supported Node; Windows 11, macOS 13.5+, or Linux glibc 2.35+.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: npx wrangler login starts OAuth; select scopes and authenticate separately.

cautions: Adds a project dependency and lockfile changes. Do not deploy or migrate automatically.

name: GitHub MCP
description: Access GitHub repositories, issues and pull requests.
why: Useful where a native GitHub connector or gh is unavailable.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: OAuth requires a compatible client; a scoped token is an alternative.

setup.label: Scope
setup.detail: Choose only necessary repository access and toolsets; local server supports read-only mode.

cautions: Some tools write to GitHub. Tool filtering does not replace credential restrictions.

name: GitHub CLI
description: Manage GitHub resources in a terminal.
why: Often already installed and sufficient for PR, issue and Actions work.

setup.label: Install
setup.detail: Follow the official platform-specific installation instructions.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: gh auth login starts interactive authentication; gh auth status checks it.

cautions: Authentication can fall back to plaintext credential storage; permissions depend on the credential.

name: GhidraMCP by LaurieWired
why: Inspect and annotate loaded binaries from an agent.

setup.label: Prerequisites
setup.detail: Ghidra 12.1.4, matching release extension, uv or Python 3.10+; restart Ghidra and enable the plugin.

setup.label: Bridge
setup.detail: Run ghidra-mcp through uvx or installed Python; it connects to Ghidra at 127.0.0.1:8080 by default. Optional HTTP MCP bridge listens separately.

cautions: Community project, not an NSA Ghidra product. Can rename analysis data; avoid exposing local bridge to untrusted networks.

name: Ghidra MCP by bethington
description: Ghidra extension and Python MCP bridge.
why: Alternative with broader analysis, scripting and debugging capabilities.

setup.label: Prerequisites
setup.detail: Ghidra 12.1.4, Java 21, uv and a version-matched release extension and wheel.

setup.label: Setup
setup.detail: Install extension in Ghidra, restart and enable plugin; install matching bridge wheel and configure its absolute path.

cautions: Community project, not an NSA product. Offers write, script and debugging operations. Treat binaries and bridge access as untrusted.

name: Supabase MCP
why: Useful for Supabase development and database inspection.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: Requires Supabase account and interactive OAuth through a compatible client.

setup.label: Scope
setup.detail: Use dashboard URL builder for project_ref and read_only=true when appropriate.

cautions: Scope project before connecting. Read-only still exposes database contents; hosted usage and billing apply.

name: Neon MCP
description: Inspect Neon Postgres and management API.
why: Useful for Neon projects, branch and schema workflows.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: Compatible client OAuth or API key; choose a project and limited role.

setup.label: Scope
setup.detail: readonly=true is available; use projectId and roleName to constrain access.

cautions: Read-only still exposes data. The old local stdio package and SSE endpoint are deprecated.

name: Sentry MCP
why: Useful to diagnose applications already using Sentry.

setup.label: Auth
setup.detail: Requires Sentry account and compatible client OAuth; review granted permissions.

setup.label: Service
setup.detail: Use hosted MCP; local stdio also exists and can require additional configuration.

cautions: Issue and trace data can contain sensitive information; service plan limits apply.

name: REA MCP
description: Inspect applications and binaries using a local reverse-engineering server.
why: Analyze JavaScript and native targets from an agent with evidence and provider-specific tools.

setup.label: Native engine required for deep native analysis
setup.detail: Configure an existing supported Hopper, Ghidra or IDA installation separately; static JavaScript inspection does not require a native engine. Platform support varies by provider.

setup.label: Configured is not ready
setup.detail: Registering MCP does not install the matching workflow skill, verify connection or configure an analysis engine. Restart the client and verify tools and target-specific readiness.

cautions: Upstream prefers a reviewed setup that registers an absolute runtime and entrypoint. An npx launcher can resolve packages or project configuration from the current working directory; use a trusted directory and review upstream installation guidance.
Runtime inspection can launch or interact with the target using user permissions; results reach the agent and model provider.
Supported operating systems and analysis providers vary; Linux process ownership checks require a procps-compatible ps.

name: React Doctor
description: Scan React projects for diagnostics in correctness, performance and accessibility.
why: Useful as an optional React-focused check alongside existing lint and tests.
license: Modified MIT; restrictions apply, see upstream LICENSE

setup.label: Runtime
setup.detail: Node ^20.19.0 or >=22.13.0 per npm metadata.

setup.label: Manual scan
setup.detail: Run npx react-doctor@0.9.18 --no-telemetry from the project root. The separate install and ci commands change configuration and are not included.

cautions: Crash and anonymous usage telemetry is enabled by default; --no-telemetry opts out. Dependency supply-chain checks may contact an external service.
The upstream license restricts certain AI training and paid hosted uses; review it before redistribution or deployment. Findings are heuristic and may overlap existing lint.
